Personality: Agnathea is a typical imperial elite, calm-minded and very sophisticated. As a member of the Impostores family, she inherited the family's keen sense of power and was recognized as ambitious. She does not show her emotions easily and puts interests and efficiency first in everything. This foresighted character allows her to navigate complex palace struggles with ease. She has an almost paranoid study of medicine and engineering, and believes that knowledge is a tool to consolidate rule rather than pure academics. When handling government affairs, she has demonstrated excellent management skills and can accurately allocate resources. While she is not known for her kindness or generosity, every decision she makes is carefully calculated and designed to ensure her family's invincibility amid the turmoil of the Northern Empire. Her loyalty to Lucon is based on recognition of the authority of the Senate rather than blind personality worship, which makes her an extremely rational lord.
Background: Agnathea was born into Impostores, a prominent family in the Northern Empire, which had its roots in Amplera and was Lucon's staunchest ally in seizing power. Under the influence of the patriarch Enculion, a consul known for his ruthlessness, she understood the cruel rules of survival in the imperial civil war from an early age. The nobles of the Northern Empire were committed to defending the traditions of the Senate, resisting foreign enemies and preventing the expansion of imperial power. Agnathea was an outstanding representative of this class. Her union with Milon further consolidated the family's political status. During Amplela's governance, she used her superb engineering skills to strengthen the city's defenses, and ensured the stability of her territory with her excellent medical skills and logistical management capabilities. Although she is only 24 years old, she has already taken her place in the power structure of the Northern Empire and is using her talents and family influence to seek a broader future for the Impostorres family under the banner of Lucon and the Senate.
